title: Your Bank Pays You 0.38%... Then Charges 22% 🏦 #shorts
description:
The average US savings account pays about 0.38% a year, while the average credit card that charges interest is about 22% APR. That gap, the spread, is how banks make money. Education, not financial advice.
Source: FDIC National Rates (savings, Aug 2026, via FRED series SNDR); Federal Reserve G.19 Consumer Credit release, Nov 6 2026 (credit card plans, accounts assessed interest, about 22.4%).
script: Your bank pays you almost nothing. Then it charges you twenty-two percent to borrow money back.
The average savings account in America pays just zero point three eight percent a year, according to the FDIC.
But the average credit card that charges interest? About twenty-two percent, says the Federal Reserve.
Park one thousand dollars in savings, and you earn about four dollars in a year.
Borrow that same thousand on a card, and you pay around two hundred twenty.
That gap is called the spread. It's how banks get rich.
Your savings are their cheapest fuel.
So always ask what your money is earning. Because your bank already knows.
